name: TSMC’s N7+ EUV FinFET process
description: TSMC adapted its N7 FinFET foundry process to use extreme ultraviolet lithography for selected layers and delivered customer products on that variant.

date.label: Q2 2019
date.basis: The foundry dates the onset of volume production to the second quarter, without giving a month.

events.statement: TSMC began volume manufacture on the N7+ process with EUV.
events.caveats: Neither a worldwide priority claim nor the use of EUV for every layer follows.

evidence.supports: The foundry dates the start to Q2 2019 and describes the relation to base N7.

evidence.locator: Opening and We Are All In
evidence.supports: The former TSMC lithography lead quotes the 2019 enhanced N7 volume ramp and describes ASML scanner work underlying the foundry’s EUV effort.

date.label: by 7 October 2019
date.basis: The 7 October announcement describes shipments as already underway.

events.statement: Customer products using N7+ were reaching the market in high volume.

evidence.supports: The release describes customer products already reaching the market.

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest volume-manufacturing date within the retained evidence is bounded to Q2 2019.

unresolved.note: A line-by-line foundry record naming NXE submodels used on volume N7+ wafers has not been located. ASML and TSMC’s documented NXE qualification programme establishes relevant background.

links.statement: N7+ used base N7 as its process foundation and introduced EUV in place of some immersion patterning.
links.scope: Within TSMC’s N7 family, selective EUV insertion and production learning.

evidence.supports: The foundry explicitly identifies base N7 as the process on which N7+ was built.

evidence.locator: Printed pp. 3–4, C. C. Wei prepared remarks on N7 and N7+
evidence.supports: Contemporaneous technical remarks describe the replacement of selected immersion layers and the continued use of most equipment.
The programme participant independently documents the enhanced 7 nm process and EUV insertion using the 2019 research presentations.
